title: Place a table's rows on the map from officer-stated coordinate columns and system
gap: AUD2 AUDIT.md gap 3: a CSV or XLSX with lat/lon or WKT columns never reached the map
qualification: Partial: offline protocol, contract and two real inputs; no Docker or runtime rehearsal

commits.subject: feat(tc1): place a read table's rows on the map from officer-stated columns and system

design: The officer opens Place on the map on an item already read as a table, picks an x/longitude and a y/latitude column or one WKT column from the read headers, and types the EPSG code; nothing is preselected and a missing code is refused with a question (422 TABLE_PLACEMENT_CRS_UNSTATED) before any write.

POST /api/v1/ingestion/cases/{caseId}/intake/items/{itemId}/table-placement checks the code with the geo service and queues one fenced job, intake-table-geojson, pinned to the table source, its revision, hash and table read (lane table; a workbook reserves scratch).

writeTableGeojson streams the original through the existing readTableWindows (10,000-row windows) and writes one Feature per placeable row: the row's columns as properties, tableRow {sourceId, sourceRevision, sha256, row}, the stated system as the collection crs member; no reprojection.

Rows with no coordinates, non-numeric text, text that is not WKT of a point/line/polygon, or a workbook cell without a stored value are skipped and counted by reason, never placed at 0,0; points stay points, WKT polygons stay polygons.

The job measures, keeps the derivative through the large-original receipt (second streamed read, SHA-256 checked), records lineage in sources.inspection.tableDerivative and enrols it with IntakeService.register on the streamed GeoJSON path; officer words read e.g. 'Placed 326 rows on the map; 80 rows skipped: 80 had no coordinates.'

open: No Docker or runtime rehearsal: the job, receipt and enrolment are proven offline with fakes and the real readers; runtimeEvidence for the route stays pending in the operation manifest.
For a workbook sheet item the words are written on the workbook's own item (the source's root item), not the sheet row.
The table is read twice (measure, then keep); a very large table costs two streamed reads.
The derivative goes no further than the existing large GeoJSON path takes any dropped file: WKT polygons become footprints only through that path's normal layout step, and points stay points.
